chief_complaint: pelvic pain, syncope, BP 80/50, missed period 6 weeks
hpi_details: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with pelvic pain, syncope, bp 80/50, missed period 6 weeks. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she is suffering from an unusually delayed, severe menstrual cramp or an ovarian cyst that burst.
concerns: She is worried that internal bleeding will permanently damage her reproductive organs and stop her from having a baby.
expectations: She hopes to get an immediate ultrasound to check what ruptured and IV fluids so she stops fainting.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes immediate resuscitation with two large-bore IVs, type and crossmatch, and emergent OR transfer for surgery in Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Ovarian cyst rupture without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

teaching.one_liner: A pregnancy outside the uterus ruptures, causing sudden pelvic pain, syncope, and hemorrhagic shock.

history.answer: My lower belly hurts terribly, and I passed out at home earlier today.
The pain started as a dull ache two days ago, but this morning it suddenly became sharp and unbearable.
It started low on my right side, but now it feels like it spreads across my entire lower abdomen.
My right shoulder started aching when I lie back flat, but the pain does not go down into my legs.
It is a severe, sharp, stabbing pain that stays constant and does not come in waves.
Right now it is an eight or nine out of ten, which is much worse than when it first began.
Any movement, coughing, or pressing on my stomach makes it much worse, and nothing relieves it.
No, I have never experienced severe pelvic pain like this in my life.
I felt sick to my stomach and threw up some clear fluid once when the pain got intense, with no blood.
My bowel movements have been normal, and I haven't had any diarrhea, constipation, or blood in my stool.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or body aches at all.
No, my eyes and skin are not yellow, and my stool has its normal brown color.
I don't have any burning when I urinate, no blood in my urine, and no need to pee more often.
When I stood up to go to the bathroom this morning, the room spun, and I collapsed and lost consciousness for a few seconds.
I have had light dark-brown spotting on a pad for the past two days, but no heavy bleeding or unusual discharge.
I don't have chest pain, but I feel slightly winded and lightheaded because my heart is beating very fast.
I only had a slice of toast and some water this morning, with no fatty food or alcohol.
I took one acetaminophen pill about an hour ago, but it did not help the pain at all.
No, I have never had an irregular heartbeat, blood clots, or any heart condition.
My last normal period was six weeks ago, so my cycle is about two weeks overdue.
I had one normal vaginal birth five years ago without complications, and no previous miscarriages or tubal pregnancies.
I am sexually active only with my husband, and we have not been using any birth control recently.
My period was several weeks late, so I thought this was just an agonizing cramp or maybe an ovarian cyst bursting.
We have been trying to get pregnant, and I am terrified that whatever is bleeding inside will ruin my chances of having a baby.
I hope you can do a quick ultrasound to see what happened inside and give me fluids so I stop passing out.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital stays other than delivering my daughter.
I do not take any prescription medications, vitamins, or herbal remedies.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked or used tobacco products.
I only drink a glass of wine socially on rare occasions, and none recently.
I work as an office manager and live with my husband and five-year-old daughter.
There is no family history of early heart disease, blood clotting disorders, or gynecologic cancers.

exam.finding: Patient appears acutely ill, pale, diaphoretic, and in severe distress due to lower abdominal pain.
Blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg, heart rate 118 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Marked conjunctival pallor bilaterally; sclerae are clear without jaundice.
Abdomen is mildly distended with no surgical scars, ecchymoses, or visible pulsations.
Hypoactive bowel sounds heard across all four quadrants.
Severe tenderness and involuntary muscular guarding over the right lower quadrant and suprapubic region.
Marked rebound tenderness elicited over the right lower quadrant and lower abdomen.
Exquisite tenderness at McBurney's point with guarding, but negative psoas and obturator signs.
No tenderness elicited on percussion over either costovertebral angle.
Exquisite cervical motion tenderness and marked right adnexal tenderness with palpable fullness; scant dark blood in the vaginal vault.
